newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel begins opening disputed Hebron street.
newsitem.headline: Israel begins opening disputed Hebron street.

text.p: Israel on Sunday partially reopened a street in the heart of Hebron closed to Palestinian traffic two years ago, PLO officials said.
Opening the street has been one of the key Palestinian demands in talks on implementing a long-delayed handover by Israel of most of the West Bank town.
Witnesses said Israeli bulldozers removed the cement blockades at entrances to al-Shuhada (martyrs) street. But they said Israeli troops still barred Palestinian traffic.

"We were informed by the Israelis on Saturday night that they would work on the gradual reopening of the street, and they would start by removing the cement blocks," a PLO official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said.

Ali al-Qawasmeh, Palestinian Minister of Communications, said: "This is one step in the reopening of the street. The Palestinians have stressed that without reopening it, we can't sign any protocol on Hebron."

The Hebron street was closed in February 1994 after a Jewish settler massacred 29 Arabs at al-Ibrahimi mosque, also known as the Tomb of the Patriarchs, in Hebron. The site is revered by Moslems and Jews. Most of the fortified enclaves in which the 400 Jews of Hebron live amidst its 100,000 Palestinians are along al-Shuhada street.
Two months of PLO-Israeli talks on implementing the Hebron handover have not resolved other key elements of the deal.
U.S. and Egyptian efforts to clinch a deal have been stepped up, with those countries aiding the sides in drafting documents they hope might narrow gaps, PLO officials said.
